lines.text: (When will this class ever end?)
(The hallway is full of the sound of another class being dismissed. Just hearing it makes my legs want to move.)
(During reading comprehension, teachers love telling us to go back and find evidence.)
(But when I look back and discover that the clues were already there, I am always startled.)
(The shadows of the trees outside the window sway for a moment.)
(Y-City in the afternoon is bright to the point of whiteness, the buildings as if copied once by the sun.)
(A copy is always a little paler than the original.)
This course is still very expensive. One class costs several hundred.
That must be a full day's wages for my parents.
The air conditioner makes a sound that is working very hard but has no dignity.
((Past perfect tense.))
(Had done.)
(English actually allows something to happen in the past of the past.)
(A lost bee is bumping against the windowpane, and some students are distracted by it.)
(A bird flashes through the shade of the trees outside. The sun is beginning to set.)
(What if gravity was reversed? We would be standing on the ceiling, having class while sitting on the rafters.)
(Outside the window)
(The summer light is so dense it almost seems solid. The classroom is still cool, hiding behind the walls, but everything exposed to the sun is so dazzling you have to close your eyes.)
(They say summer is the best season, and childhood is the best time of life.)
(Yes, I agree completely. I can already see myself as a frail old person in the winter of my life, lost in thought, wishing a million times I could come back to this very moment.)
(But right now, on this day when the sun is at its most fierce, what should we do, so as not to have wasted our time?)
(The Tyndall effect appears in the gap of the curtains. Dust motes, usually invisible, dance in the column of light.)
(The teacher's voice is gradually fading.)
(I wish Y-City had white nights. Here, people have to go home by 8 PM, be in bed by 10 PM, and by 11 PM the streets are empty except for lonely wandering souls.)
(If Julian was really as successful abroad as he claims, why would he come back to our second-tier city to teach middle school English?)
(*Beyond English, Beyond Yourself.*)
(Transcend English, transcend yourself.)
(But when we truly transcend English, what will we use to express our emotions?)
(And when we truly transcend ourselves, what do we become? Something other than ourselves?)
(Yuanyuan is still memorizing vocabulary, completely absorbed.)
(Actually, vocabulary might not even be that important. When you read, you can just substitute words with their first letter.)
(Mr. J teaches in Y-City, and Ms. Y teaches in J-City. Most nouns in the world are irrelevant. You could replace them with pictures.)
(Adjectives and adverbs can play a key role, but most of the time, you can do without them. The () Mr. J teaches () in the () Y-City. No one would care.)
(Today, while Julian was talking her ear off, Minna just kept a polite smile. Her eyes were actually on the water cooler at the end of the hallway.)
(Some dreams do not die when you grow up. They only)
(turn into nouns you rarely mention.)
(Botanist.)
(A job that requires crossing mountains and rivers.)
(The age of great global discoveries has already passed.)
(Physics, chemistry, and biology were better suited to the last century, or the century before that.)
(Now those fields only need small repairs.)
Is a failed hobby still a hobby?
(I like drawing.)
(But like is a very safe word, because it does not have to become what I want to be in the future.)
(Come to think of it, Y-City is also a UN livable city.)
(I do not understand why. If the inspection team had come in summer, they would not have)
(said that.)
(If we are talking about new things in Y-City,)
(then it would probably be H Mall.)
(H Mall has some brands you used to only see online.)
(Starbucks, Uniqlo, and Muji are all here.)
(I do not dislike it either, but after walking around too much, I feel a little lost. After all, we only buy some stationery and leave.)
(But Cici loves browsing places like this and talks about it with great excitement every time.)
Why was Linda unable to buy her apple pie?
(Some things are not missed because I did not try hard enough. It is just that by the time we finally have time,)
(the stall has already closed.)
(A tiny miss can lead to a huge mistake.)
(Ordinary can also be an adjective.)
Julian asks where I usually go after class.
I would say home.
Honestly, I do not know how to start writing.
Why do we always have units like this?
Why are there always forms at school asking for household registration and parents' workplaces?
Even if my parents never said it, I know.
For workplace, write it truthfully. For occupation, just write employee.
(Writing it this way is always safe. Teachers and classmates will not be able to guess the details.)
My father is strict.
He always says he is good at math.
But my math is an absolute mess.
I always calculate things wrong. I do not know why.
Good thing his English is good.
His English is completely awful.
Thinking of that makes me feel much better.
My mom is supportive, but only of the things she wants to support.
Doctor, teacher, those are all good occupations.
If I get the chance, I will become a teacher.
Too many children need my help.
Julian is much more responsible than the teachers at school.
The English teachers at school teach English class in Chinese.
Looking at the answer key is more useful than listening to them...
Why do the texts always have strange relatives?
After the typhoon passed, my mood also improved a lot.
Seeing everything beaten down equally by the rain, losing its order,
finally let me put down some of the weight in my heart.
There is a small puddle of rainwater on the windowsill. It is slowly drying.
The classroom smells damp.
Summer is already half over,
but everything is still at its height, as if it will never end.
Every morning I wake up to inexhaustible sunlight.
Outdoor work can start before the sun comes up and rest at noon.
But indoor work cannot do that.
It can only rely on air conditioning.
Not enough air conditioning is obviously hopeless.
But too much, like here at Beyond English, is not good either. You have to bring an extra layer when you come in.
Cici is hiding something from me.
That feeling is awful.
She is doing a terrible job pretending otherwise.
If Cici is gone, who will go to school with me?
Why complain that studying is tiring?
Do you not understand what happens if you do not study?
It is okay to fall apart.
I was once like this too.
If Cici is gone, who will walk home from school with me?
If Cici is gone, who will spend breaks with me?
If Cici is gone, who will eat with me?
Why do I always fail to meet friends who are ambitious?
You are drawn to their ease.
Why does every friend I have live so easily...
They have never faced a moment of life or death!
Is that not also a kind of happiness? You should bless them.
Why not take an expensive cram school seriously? With that money and time, would it not be better to do something else?
